column1: Formatting tags used across paragraph breaks get closed at end of paragraph
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2015 Revision 3304 If a tag is open across a paragraph break, eg: Here is where my italics start and then! Here is where they end. After we put in the paragraph tags, Nokogiri will very helpfully close the first tag at the end of the paragraph, and then ditch the unmatched close-tag, so we end up with:

Here is where my italics start and then!

Here is where they end.

This is not desirable obviously. :'(
column125: 15/Nov/10 9:41 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Test with deferred bit for this issue committed in revision 3310.
column127:

column128:
21/Nov/10 5:09 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Fixed in revision 3365.

The formatting tags b big cite code del em i s small strike strong sub sup tt u should
now all be closed and re-opened around inserted paragraph breaks, as long as they are
properly closed in the user's input. (If the tag is just unclosed, we let Nokogiri
close it at the end of the next paragraph like it wants to, since otherwise we'd be
opening and closing the tags at every paragraph break in the entire document.) 

Have added a bit more testing to the parser feature, but this could use some more broken
input, and testing in the RTE especially. 
- **Status changed**: `FixedAndCommitted`
column130:

Also worked on edit, i.e. when I tried to add formatting across paragraphs with the
p tags already in place. Parser closed and opened the formatting tag correctly on preview.
And also worked when I added em tags across paragraphs to text that was already correctly
tagged with p and strong.

column1: Duplicated xml causing problems with epubs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2026 What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number in the footer). 3328 If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen: What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. Download an epub to a problem-intolerant device. 2. Find it is broken. In the work.xml file portion of the epub, xmlns=“www.w3.org/1999/xhtml” and xml:lang=“en” are each defined twice in the epub source, and so some of the xml parsers aren’t liking that.

From my end, if I edit it to remove those two duplicates, then it works on my software ereader where it wasn’t previously working. So I’m 99% sure that’s the big problem. If you could use more troubleshooting details; I love my epubs and am happy to spend the time to get this fixed.

column149:
02/Dec/17 3:19 PM;557058:dc27adcc-12e8-41ee-aef8-0e63f2a87cb3;searched for works with 0 words in every language, and the only ones that seemed to have 0 words were the ones that were fan art/video, or some sort of glitchy media that resulted in text like ".........." and nothing else. also tried making a new work in chinese with no spaces, and this still results in a word count of 1. as far as nonroman languages go, it's rare to have absolutely no spacing or line breaks in text, and even if this were the case, works that are not text based at all will display a word count of 0, so works like that will still exist regardless of the language.

also, for languages like chinese and japanese, character count is not reflective of "word count" quite the way it is in english, since each character in a line does not necessarily form a whole word alone... this issue extends beyond coding considerations, and for the sake of being consistent and keeping things simple, as a user i'd prefer that work blurbs either show both word & character count for all works, or not at all. having some works show word count and some show character count, or only have some show both, would be a lot more confusing i think. if it were up to me i'd say: don't do anything about this.
column150:
17/Oct/18 2:27 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;A note for the future from our Chinese translation team, in case we want to implement this as well:

{quote}Not only characters, punctuation also counts as “word” in Chinese. Punctuation, such as “……” or “——“, is even regarded as 2 “words”.

So word count of a Chinese article that contains English words = number of Chinese characters \+ Number of English words \+ number of punctuation.

{quote}
column151:
17/Oct/18 7:54 PM;557058:ac875cf3-3d39-4f16-ac14-8ab622615dea;Thanks for pointing it out\! I forgot to add a comment that this implementation doesn’t include punctuation. 02/Nov/18 9:58 PM;557058:77351d0c-19f2-456d-8c3f-39bc145cb6dd;Testing for Japanese:

Each kanji character counts as one word
Each hiragana character counts as one word
Each katakana character counts as one word
Spacing doesn't affect word count; punctuation is not counted.
Words in roman characters mixed in count normally (that is, each group of roman characters separated by a space is one word, as well as each group of roman characters separated by at least one Japanese character).

It's this method that adds the error early on:

  before_validation :check_synonym
  def check_synonym
    if !self.new_record? && self.name_changed?
      # ordinary wranglers can change case and accents but not punctuation or the actual
letters in the name
      # admins can change tags with no restriction
      unless User.current_user.is_a?(Admin) || (self.name.downcase == self.name_was.downcase)
|| (self.name.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s == self.name_was.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s)
        self.errors.add(:name, "can only be changed by an admin.")
      end
    end
    if self.merger_id
      if self.canonical?
        self.errors.add(:base, "A canonical can't be a synonym")
      end
      if self.merger_id == self.id
        self.errors.add(:base, "A tag can't be a synonym of itself.")
      end
      unless self.merger.class == self.class
        self.errors.add(:base, "A tag can only be a synonym of a tag in the same category
as itself.")
      end
    end
  end

At that point, merger_id *isn't* nil, even if the syn_string is blank, and the "synonym
of" (the merger) would be removed somewhere in the next steps, where the method syn_string=
is applied:

 def syn_string=(tag_string)
    if tag_string.blank?
      self.merger_id = nil
    else
  # etc.

Don't know yet what would be the best way to rejigger.

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2076 As of revision 3419, users can now create work skins (custom stylesheets) which they can apply to their stories to make custom formatting for others. - Users should be able to create new work skins from their dashboard under the "My Skins" option. - Any work skins created should automatically have all the elements preceded with ".userstuff" even if the user doesn't put it in (this is what keeps the effects jailed to just the user's own text). - Users should be able to set class attributes (eg

) in their HTML as long as these class names are alphanumeric with underscores and dashes. - Users should be able to view their own and public work skins. - Users should not be able to view non-public work skins by others. - Users should be able to select their own or an approved public skin in the Post New work form from a pull-down menu above the work text. - If a work skin has been applied to a given work, the "Hide Creator's Style" button should appear at the top of the page for all readers, whether logged in or not. - If the "Hide Creator's Style" button is pressed, it should remove all effects of the work skin and replace the button with "Show Creator's Style" - Users should be able to set a preference to always hide creator's style/custom work style, in which case they will see the "Show Creator's Style" button as an option on works that have a custom stylesheet. Note that user work skins can be approved for public use just like user site skins, but I would generally recommend against doing this very often since it will clutter the pull-down list in the work new form.

Behavior appears to be browser-independent.  Tested in Macintosh Safari 5.0.3, Firefox
16.0.2, Chrome 22.0.1229.94, Opera 12.02

New chapters:

Choose “Add Chapter”, put text in the chapter, “Preview”, return to editing the chapter
with either “Edit Chapter” or “Edit”, change the text, and “Preview” again.

--Changes will not appear in the preview.
--Using the top “Post Chapter” button will post WITHOUT the changes
--Using the top “Edit Chapter” button will return you to editing WITHOUT the changes
--Using the bottom “Post” button will post WITH the changes
--Using the bottom “Edit” button will return you to editing the chapter WITH the changes

All previews have "This is a preview of what this chapter will look like when it's
posted to the Archive. You should probably read the whole thing to check for problems
before posting." message and gray background behind text.

Editing existing chapters:

All previews have "This is a preview of what this chapter will look like when it's
posted to the Archive. You should probably read the whole thing to check for problems
before posting." message BUT are missing gray background behind text.

--Behavior is identical as when adding new chapters except that when previewing there
is no "Post Chapter" button.  "Edit Chapter" returns one to editing WITHOUT one's changes,
"Edit" returns one to editing WITH one's changes, and "Update" (the only posting choice)
posts WITH one's changes.

Related tickets:
https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/243504
https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/243102

Another issue involving different behavior from "Post Chapter" and "Post": http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=3306

01/Mar/13 3:41 AM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;Posting the first chapter of a work, the Preview has buttons "Post", "Save Work Draft",
"Edit", and "Cancel".

"Post" posts the work.
"Save Work Draft" saves it as a draft.  If you edit a draft and Preview, there is now
a button for "Save Work Draft", which updates your draft with your changes.
"Edit" returns one to editing.  If you make text changes and Preview again, the changes
are visible.  (Tag changes are not - see Issue 3461)
"Cancel" gives message "New work posting canceled."  Work is not posted and no draft
is created.

Adding and then Previewing a chapter other than the first, you get this blue message:

"This is a draft showing what this chapter will look like when it's posted to the Archive.
You should probably read the whole thing to check for problems before posting. The
chapter draft will be stored until you post or discard it, or until its parent work
is deleted."

The background is gray.  There is only one set of buttons, at the bottom.  They are
"Post", "Edit", "Keep Draft", "Discard Draft".

"Post" posts the chapter.
**"Edit" returns one to editing.  If you make text changes and Preview again, the changes
are NOT visible, although they are present in the Work Text window if you choose "Edit"
again, and are posted if you choose "Post".**
"Keep Draft" creates a draft chapter.
"Discard Draft" discards the chapter, not saving a draft.

Editing an existing chapter of a multi-chapter work and Previewing gives gray background,
buttons "Update", "Edit", "Cancel".

"Update" posts the chapter with any added changes.
**"Edit" returns one to editing.  If you make text changes and Preview again, the changes
are NOT visible, although they are present in the Work Text window if you choose "Edit"
again, and are posted if you choose "Post".**
"Cancel" exits editing and discards changes.

Button changes are definitely an improvement and the issue of lost content is gone,
but text edits to chapters on a multi-chapter work are still not visible upon Preview,
so marking BOT.- **Status changed**: `BrokenOnTest-DeployBlocking`

column134:
22/Jan/20 1:06 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The reason this is happening: if you call {{redirect_back_or_default}} in an action that doesn't have {{skip_before_action :store_location}}, then {{redirect_back_or_default}} will try to redirect to the _current_ URL, because that was the location most recently stored.

When deleting a related work, the URL is the same as the URL for showing that related work (just with a different HTTP method). Which means that the call to {{redirect_back_or_default}} in {{RelatedWorksController#destroy}} always tries to redirect to the related work that was just deleted.

I think this can be addressed by adding {{skip_before_action :store_location, only: [:destroy]}} to the header of the {{RelatedWorksController}}. Or by using {{redirect_back}}, so that it relies on the {{Referer}} header instead of the location stored in the session cookies.

12/Mar/20 12:40 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I think this is exclusively a caching issue at this point. If you delete a user, and then call {{work.touch}} (to change {{work.cache_key}}) and {{Rails.cache.delete("works/\#\{work.id\}/guest_kudos_count")}}, the kudos list on that work updates to show the right number of user/guest kudos. (Some kudos counts used to be calculated using a {{COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address)}} query, which resulted in kudos with no {{pseud_id}} and no {{ip_address}} disappearing. But as far as I can tell, [the counts haven’t been calculated that way since 2012|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/commit/2b04876f80c81161f5d8029b2b108ff9ecb2131f], so I’m pretty sure it’s been a caching problem ever since.)

column1: Clean up kudos on chapters and remove chapter validations from the kudo model
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
A long time ago (before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2194#icft=AO3-2194|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2194#icft=AO3-2194|smart-link]), users were able to leave kudos on chapters, before we changed things so kudos can only be left on works. There are remaining traces of this feature we should remove:

* Add a task to find all chapter kudos and transfer them to works. If the transfer failed (because the same user/IP address has also left kudos on the work), simply remove the chapter kudos.
* Remove kudos validation code that loads chapters ([creator check|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/kudo.rb#L57-L67], [guests on restricted works check|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/kudo.rb#L76-L85]).
* Add kudos validation for the presence and the type of the commentable, similar to [what we did with subscribables|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/subscription.rb#L11-L15] ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5008#icft=AO3-5008|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5008#icft=AO3-5008|smart-link]).

How to test:

* (Server admin) Test the rake task.
** Get the number of chapter kudos on staging.
** Find one work with a chapter kudo (from user A).
** Run the task.
** Check that there are no chapter kudos on staging.
** Check that the example work still has kudos from user A.
* (Anyone)
** Check that you cannot leave kudos on your own work. You can do this by logging in as someone else, opening your own work, and then logging in as yourself in a new tab and attempting to kudos the work in the original tab
** Check that as a guest, you cannot leave kudos on a restricted work. You can do this by opening the work in a private tab, then change the work to restricted in another tab, then return to the first tab to leave guest kudos. You’ll get a generic error message this way, not a specific one about the work being restricted, but it’s fine. (Alternately, you can use inspect element to change the commentable ID of an arbitrary kudos form to get the more specific error message, e.g. “You can't leave guest kudos on a restricted work.“)

*Deploy notes*

{{bundle exec rake After:clean_up_chapter_kudos}}

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2218
New feature: prompt meme challenges

A new challenge type, instead of being a gift exchange, a challenge can be a prompt
meme. This will allow things like fic_promptly or comment_fic to run on the AO3, or
various other memes.

Basic workflow:
Mod creates a new prompt meme challenge
Users sign up with one or several prompts, which can be public or anonymous
Users can then claim prompts, to indicate they are intending to fill them
Several users can claim the same prompt, and it will show if this has happened
Users can then post to fulfil their claims, and it will fill in the request details
automatically
This will then show on the list of claims as fulfilled.
Mod can make challenge unrevealed or anonymous-writers just as for a gift exchange.

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tag_wranglers

When an admin removes wrangling permissions from a user, the wrangler's fandoms still
remain assigned to that wrangler, but the wrangler doesn't turn up on the Wrangler
drop-down list anymore (making it difficult to remove those fandoms from the wrangler.)
E.g. when I remove permissions from my Xparrot wrangler account, "Xparrot" no longer
appears in the "Filter by Wrangler" dropdown on http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tag_wranglers
- but Xparrot is still the wrangler listed on all fandoms.

This is useful behavior in one respect (since it means even if a wrangler's permissions
accidentally get removed, they'll still retain their fandoms) but the de-commissioned
wranglers should still be listed in the drop-down, so their fandoms can be removed.

(Low-priority fix since there's an easy workaround, to simply restore permissions long
enough to unassigned the wrangler's fandoms.)

Non-canonical tags with 0 use counts in works/drafts/etc should get raked, but various
unused tags on the Archive are lingering like zombies. 

The tag itself lists 0 works, but if searched for:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&query[name]=jhon+c*&query[type]=
the tag shows (1) use.

According to elz: "the rake task checks the taggings_count column, because that's a
lot faster than counting the uses for each tag; the taggings_count column is *supposed*
to be incremented automatically by Rails, but they got out of sync".

column130:
28/Sep/12 3:43 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Solution, with Elz's approval - manually update the taggings_count table to match the
current tag use count whenever "Save changes" is hit on a Tag Edit page.

(Since there are too many tags on the archive to reset all of them, this will allow
wranglers to fix individual tags as we come across them.  And since only about half
of tag wrangling is done from the tag edit page anyway, this shouldn't cause too much
server strain.)

Note for testers: this feature may be difficult to test on Test, because afaik there's
no way to make a mis-counted tag deliberately; testers either will just have to find
one, or else save testing for Beta.

column27:

in ChallengeAssignmentsController

  def generate
    # regenerate assignments using the current potential matches
    ChallengeAssignment.generate!(@collection)
    redirect_to collection_potential_matches_path(@collection)
  end
  

This ChallengeAssignment.generate! method can take a long time for a big collection
like yuletide or remix. If the unicorn worker is killed, it leaves the assignments
in a partially completed state.

The process needs to be backgrounded, with a message saying that it's in progress,
and an email sent when it's done, similar to the way PotentialMatches.generate! is
handled.

1. Try to import a story from http://www.the-archive.net/index.php (any story).
2. Get gibberish and script tags, but no story.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Since it's not a known source, I'd expect the whole body of the page to be imported.

The problem is that the source includes a special character, "non SGML character number
0", according to the W3 Validator, and Nokogiri sees it as a string terminator (which
it is, in C and probably other languages) and stops processing there.

column1: Reusing invitation can expose original invitee's email
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2269
What archive revision are you testing on?
Release 0.8.6

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Use the Send invite function from the interface to send an invite to an email address.
2. Invitation is never used.
3. Decide to give it to someone else by copy-pasting the link, and not by updating
the invite to another email address.
4. The invite is redeemed by the new invitee.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

In my Invitations management page, I see the invitation as sent to [old email] and
redeemed by [new invitee], and I can no longer edit/update it.

More importantly, the invitee has seen the old email when they were on the new user
creation page, because we set the form to fill in the email with the email associated
with the invitation.

This is, I grant it, user error - I (the user) should have updated the invite to resend
it by email.

But there are cases when you don't know the email, and people find it easier to follow
links given directly to them rather than dig for emails in the Spam bin where they
often end up. Also, the average user will have no idea that the original invitee's
email would be exposed, because they don't know our code inside out (or at all...)

So I'm just logging this so we don't forget it entirely.

column1: auto retry failed resque jobs

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2282
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.8.6.11

resque jobs fail when there's a race condition (e.g. the redis job is created for a
new kudo, but when the redis job goes to find the kudo, it's not there yet because
the database hasn't finished processing the transaction)

they need to be retried automatically.

I am currently running 

   (Resque::Failure.count-1).downto(0).each { |i| Resque::Failure.requeue(i) && Resque::Failure.remove(i)
}

in a loop from the console, but a gem such as lantins' resque-retry would be preferable

column1: Tag set editing for browsing and challenges
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2314
We want to have more sophisticated tag set editing and usage options, which should also
include nominations for challenges. 

See the detailed design here:

https://transformativeworks.basecamphq.com/projects/1378016/posts/43691445/
column127:
03/Oct/11 9:17 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;The broad strokes of what happens throughout this code.

The heart of the changes are centered around the new OwnedTagSet model, which represents
a managed and curated tag set, the kind used in a challenge. The old TagSet model remains
-- this is as before a very basic model which is just a bag of tags. TagSets are still
the "guts" of prompts and requests, and there's one that acts as the guts in each OwnedTagSet
model. However, OwnedTagSet adds a layer of complexity atop this model for management
and nomination purposes. The requirement for canonical tags in the TagSet model has
been removed. Tags must still exist, however, before being added to a TagSet, EXCEPT
if the TagSet belongs to an OwnedTagSet, in which case new tags can be created.

(There is some refactoring work to do here, btw, to improve the encapsulation of the
inner tag set, which is currently exposed in some places where tags are being added/removed
from the set. Ideally we should instead be passing through those commands to the internal
tag set transparently via method missing.)

Because the basic tag set is just an internal guts thing, I've used tag_sets for the
routing and name, to keep that inner tag set invisible to users for more clarity.

The road to the happy land of OwnedTagSets branches off on the "tags" tab, but most
users will probably come to tag sets from the challenge setup page, which links to
them where the former paste-in box was.

OwnedTagSets can have owners (who can do whatever with them) and moderators (who can
approve and reject nominations), on the theory that what someone really needs less-authorized
help with is managing a bunch of user input.

OwnedTagSets have three key prefs: whether they are visible (whether anyone can see
the tags in the set), whether they are usable (whether people other than the mods can
use it in a challenge), and whether they are taking nominations. If a tag set is taking
noms, the owner can specify the number of nominations of each type of tag.

Without nominations, the OwnedTagSet can just have tags specified manually the way
they used to be in the challenge settings form. For clarity, tags currently in the
set are listed in checkbox fields (scrolling if the number is really big) to remove.

With nominations, individual users can submit nominations for a set number of tags.
These create TagNomination objects rather than actual tags, in order to avoid polluting
our db with piles of unused tags. TagNominations try and track the state of corresponding
tags (eg, to determine whether they're canonical or not and if they have the desired
parent tag or not) and store their approved/rejected state. (It's not super-critical
if this gets out of sync as it's mainly to give the tag set mods some extra info when
deciding whether to approve/reject, so I haven't hammered on this a ton.)

Mods can then review noms and approve, reject, edit, or leave them hanging out for
a while. :) For performance reasons, a limited number of noms of any one type are shown
to users at a time. As nominations are reviewed, they clear out and new noms are displayed.

The front end will not be working until after lim's css/html revisions are merged,
but the general principles of the display and forms are:
- char/rel tags are organized under fandoms for display, and also for review if the
set includes fandom nominations
- if a set doesn't allow fandom nominations, only char/rel nominations, these will
be shown flat for review on the assumption that such a tag set is going to be for a
single-fandom (or small group of fandom) challenge.

Finally, OwnedTagSets can also include TagSetAssociations. These allow a moderator
to hook up chars/rels with fandoms in their tag set the way that wranglers do with
canonical tags, for autocomplete purposes in signup forms. There are tools for batch
loading associations and for picking through nominations to find potential associations.

The key change to challenges (aside from just the technicality of how they get hooked
up to tag sets -- prompt restrictions can now have multiple tag sets attached and pull
their tags from all of them) is in how characters and relationships are collected for
autocomplete when being done via autocomplete.

When the user picks a fandom, chars and relationships for that fandom are pulled (from
redis) from both canonical tag associations AND tag set associations. The mod can then
choose whether to show ALL of these options, or to limit the options to only the chars
and rels that are in the tag set. Basically, the mod can choose between:

*    have a bigger and more complex tag set with all characters to choose from in the
set, with the benefit of having full control over what characters might appear in the
form (useful if you want to offer "Any" as an option without worrying that the wranglers
might suddenly wrangle in some new char)

*    have a simpler tag set that only includes characters that have to be put into
tag set associations, at the cost of having characters potentially be added to the
list as the wranglers work.

column133:
22/Jan/14 11:30 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;OK, after some more testing, I can now clarify. Adding a work to a series WILL cause
its download to expire. What will NOT cause the download to expire is adding a DIFFERENT
work to the series. This causes the part # in the download to be inaccurate if the
author inserts a prequel or earlier work in a series. 

EG:

Add work "Foo" to series "Snafu" 
Download Foo: it says "Part 1 of series Snafu"
Add work "Bar" to series "Snafu" as a prequel and make it the first part
Download Bar: it says "Part 1 of series Snafu"
Download Foo again and get the cached download: it continues to say "Part 1 of series
Snafu" 

OPTIONS: 

1) only include series name information ("Part of series Y") -- fixes this issue --
and work on downloading series as a whole (issue 2939)

2) expire the downstream downloads for any series when a new work is added. -- partial
fix for this issue
PROBLEM: existing downloads will remain inaccurate. In other words, if Jane User already
has "Foo" downloaded on her computer, there is nothing whatsoever we can do to make
it say anything other than "Part 1 of series Snafu," so she still has no way of telling
which of Foo or Bar comes first unless she checks the archive manually. 

Or split down the middle: we could leave the current occasionally-inaccurate information
(with or without #2 fix) as a convenience until we implement downloading an entire
series at once, at which point we change individual works to contain "Part of series
Y" -- merge this issue into issue 2939.

column131:
27/May/12 4:17 AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;More details as background: the normal New Comment and the Reply to Comment are generated
from the same back-end code (in app/views/comments) and generate the exact same HTML
- the link to help is rendered in both cases as <a title="Html help" rel="ibox&type=3"
class="symbol question" aria-controls="#ibox" href="/help/html-help.html">.

The difference is that the Reply to Comment box is generated dynamically, but the JQuery
required to make the magic happen is only run on the original page, not the dynamically-generated
content (see http://www.dreamincode.net/forums/topic/141922-ibox-wont-load/)

I haven't found and actual solution yet - a quick fix might be to generate the reply
form for each item when the page is originally created on the back end but that would
make for a very cumbersome HTML page (so forget I even mentioned anything so silly).


I thought adding target="_blank" to the generated link might at least force the non-JS
fallback to load in a different tab, but that just breaks the whole thing and causes
the IBox to load the home page instead of the help page.

The proper solution is apparently to force JQuery to run again when a new reply form
is generated, but Googling "jquery dynamically generated content" produced solutions
I didn't really understand. It may be that someone more knowledgeable with JavaScript
and JQuery might be able to find a proper solution. It feels as though it's within
our grasp anyway.- **Status changed**: `Accepted`

column1: Autocomplete tag suggestions should not rely on user input matching the tag's diacritics, e.g. A should return results for Â and vice versa
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2383*

*What archive revision are you testing on?*
0.8.7.0

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Create a canonical tag that contains an accented character – for this issue, we have the fandom tag “ÂO3-2380” on staging
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## Fill in the Name field with a tag name with an accented character, e.g. “ÂO3-2380”
## Check “Canonical”
## Select a category, e.g. Fandom
## Press “Create Tag”
# Create a similar canonical without an accented character – for this issue, we have the fandom tag “AO3-0000” on staging
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## Fill in the Name field with a tag name with an accented character, e.g. “AO3-0000”
## Check “Canonical”
## Select a category, e.g. Fandom
## Press “Create Tag”
# Attempt to locate the first tag with the autocomplete
## Search > Works
## In the fandoms field, enter “AO” or  “ÂO”

*What is the expected output? What happens instead?*

If I type “AO,” it should suggest both “ÂO3-2380” and “AO3-0000,” but it only suggests “AO3-0000.”

If I type “ÂO,” it should suggest both “ÂO3-2380” and “AO3-0000,” but it only suggests “ÂO3-2380”

*Notes*

The solution may involve normalizing the user input and keeping normalized copies of the tags in Redis for searching. The[ code that allows wranglers to change the diacritics on a tag|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/models/tag.rb#L193] handles it like so:

{code:ruby}# ordinary wranglers can change case and accents but not punctuation or the actual letters in the name
# admins can change tags with no restriction
unless User.current_user.is_a?(Admin) || (self.name.downcase == self.name_was.downcase) || (self.name.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s == self.name_was.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s)
  self.errors.add(:name, "can only be changed by an admin.")
end{code}

*Deploy notes*

This functionality is accomplished by storing in redis autocomplete strings stripped of diacritics (in addition to the lower casing that was already happening to make it case insensitive) via {{ActiveSupport::Inflector.transliterate(string)}} and then similarly stripping diacritics from input when invoking the autocomplete. 

You will need to run the rake task {{autocomplete:reload_tag_data}} in order to get this functionality for existing tags.
column126:
12/Jun/11 5:18 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;I don't think this is a good idea, tbh. For each tag, we store it under all the possible
prefixes. EG, "Edgar" is stored under e, ed, edg, edga, edgar. If you want to show
accented-character tags, and you have Édgar, it has to be stored under e, ed, edg,
edga, edgar AS WELL AS é, éd, édg, édga, édgar. If you have a string with more than
one accented character in it, the permutations get bigger if you want to support typing
one accented character but not another. 

On top of that, lots of characters don't have an ASCII equivalent, and there's no programmatic
way that I know of to do this. We'd have to manually specify what characters to convert
and what the ASCII "fallback" character was for each one, and it would only work for
a subset. 

A better alternative IMO would be to take all synned tags and put them into the db
in completed form, so that if you typed out a noncanonical synned tag, you'd get the
canonical synonym as an autocomplete option. This wouldn't prevent ALL typos, but would
mean that typos are less likely to be repeated and perpetuated.
column127:
13/Jun/11 1:32 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;I don't entirely understand how diacritics work, but I know as a wrangler that the described
synning wouldn't work.  We can't have non-accented tags synned to accented tags, because
the database considers them the same, e.g. if there is a tag "edgar" in the database,
you cannot create a new tag "édgar" - it will insist it already exists, because it
reads "edgar" and "édgar" as the same tag.  The only way to make an "édgar" tag is
for an admin to rename the "edgar" tag using the diacritic.  So if the tag creation
database reads them as the same tag, couldn't the auto-complete do the same?
column128:
18/Jun/11 5:35 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Er, hey! that would be a big ol bug, there. "édgar" and "edgar" should both be allowed
to exist. :(

14/Jan/21 8:41 AM;5cc68d1b2f51be0e56a1ccf0;This remains an improvement that would be extremely beneficial for the work of the Tag Wrangling Committee, so I just wanted to stop in and comment with additional information regarding where the issue stands currently (given that this improvement request was added originally in 2011 and the Archive has changed substantially since then). At the time of it’s original addition, this was an improvement requested more to avoid the additional work of synning misspelled tags, today it’s more an issue concerning accessibility and practical usability both for the Tag Wrangling Committee and for users of the Archive at large.

At the present time, while the database recognizes characters with diacritics as being the same characters with or without the diacritics, the autocomplete does not. Thus neither tag search nor the autocomplete on tag landing pages or works pages will recognize, for example, Wei as being the same as Wèi and thus will not bring up results for [Wèi Yīng | Wèi Wúxiàn|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/W%C3%A8i%20Y%C4%ABng%20%7C%20W%C3%A8i%20W%C3%BAxi%C3%A0n]. This makes wrangling fandoms that make use of diacritics challenging and also makes these tags more difficult to use or to search for as a general rule. 

When the request for this improvement was initially added, the issue was considerably less prominent than it currently is and is likely to continue to be in the future since, as we welcome more fandoms to the Archive which make use of diacritics, we’re more frequently having to decide between accessibility and accuracy and inclusion when deciding whether to include diacritics in canonicals. It’s a particularly fraught issue with fandoms like The Untamed and Módào Zǔshī - Mòxiāng Tóngxiù and others which make use of diacritics for the majority of their canonicals as the fandoms are Chinese in origin, but which are also massively popular with users who read and write in a variety of different languages.

Ideally, in this improvement, we’d still like the autocomplete to function as the database functions in regards to diacritics and how it treats characters across the board so that, as in the example cited in the summary above, è is considered the same as e by the autocomplete, and brings up the same set of results.

Thank you\! ❤️

30/Aug/21 4:51 AM;5d78ea7a458a170db4b0712f;Okay, this doesn’t behave quite how I expected it to, though I imagine I don’t understand what the desired behaviour is precisely. I had assumed that this would mean the autocomplete would ignore entirely the presence or absence of a diacritic, and it appears that it doesn’t. I will describe my experiences below.

I tested this on mobile (Safari, iPhone XR), on the post new work form. I tested fandoms and characters. *The presence or absence of a diacritic did not preclude the desired tag appearing on the autocomplete, but it did affect when and where it was suggested.* I tested several names, particularly where tags with the same basic string with and without diacritics existed on staging.

I tried finding “Élisabeth de Valois | Elisabetta di Valois” by starting to type in Characters. I did not enter anything else on the form. If I typed part of her first name with the correct diacritic (e.g. “Élisab”) the suggestion would appear at the top, before other “Elisabeth”s without diacritics. It also highlighted the corresponding part of the name in the suggested tag (see image).

!4A507EDA-5993-4A98-8AD7-B511D17D400D.jpeg|width=414,height=234!

If I use the wrong diacritic (e.g. “Èlisab”) or no diacritic (“Elisab”) the behaviour is different. The autocomplete returned the same results in the same order, but highlighted “Elisab” only on tags that had the matching diacritic (see images).

!87C9CD34-5A27-4269-BB61-34C70EA55E4C.jpeg|width=414,height=204!

!EC425607-3E73-4239-9CAD-DE4051FDF836.jpeg|width=414,height=247!

About here is when I realised Élisabeth’s tag was not a great one to test on because it has a pipe with a very similar name without diacritics. So I tried on the whole name “Elisabeth” plus variations, since “Elisabetta” doesn’t match that. Then the order of results changed. Typing “Élisabeth” with the correct diacritic delivered the tag at the top (and highlighted the matching string), but typing it with the wrong diacritic or no diacritic resulted in a different order of suggested tags and the matching string not taking diacritics into account not highlighted (see images).

!669218C2-526C-4C27-9B09-B3523B32A0AF.jpeg|width=414,height=233!

!61D1BAD9-230F-447C-9277-8607C897EC78.jpeg|width=414,height=360!

!E5FCEF18-89C7-4A5C-B9F1-C09194CA0569.jpeg|width=414,height=386!

So I tested other tags\! I tried finding “La Belle et la Bête | Beauty and the Beast” (a Fandom tag) and saw the same results with Bête only being highlighted if the diacritics matched precisely. Nonetheless, the tag did show up when I typed “la bete”, “la béte”, and “la bête”. I’m not convinced it wasn’t matching on “la”, to be honest, judging by other suggestions (see image), but whatever.

!1667DF8B-C088-4BF2-96BA-10931F3F4C7D.jpeg|width=414,height=358!

Next I tried testing “Honoré” in the fandoms field, trying to pull up various Honoré de Balzac fandoms. The results were very interesting\! Searching “Honoré”, the string with the correct diacritic, pulled up the correct fandoms as well as fandoms matching “Honor”. It highlighted “Honor” in the desired fandoms (not the whole “Honoré”), and also “Honor” on the rest. Searching “Honorê”, using the wrong diacritic, appeared to search on “Honor”? It gave me the same results as the search with the correct diacritic. On the other hand, searching “Honore”, with no diacritic, only pulled up the desired Honoré de Balzac fandoms and no others, and did not highlight any part of either suggestion. See images below:

!D41E5CA7-F968-4749-9EE9-D067BB24FAB0.jpeg|width=414,height=291!

!FC85D625-B86A-440B-A7B0-F86780A4C927.jpeg|width=414,height=279!

!CA110235-6242-4792-8E18-6E0C27427774.jpeg|width=414,height=156!

Interestingly, adding a space after the above strings changes the results again. Searching “Honorê “ (note trailing space) brings up only the Balzac fandoms, and no longer the fandoms matching on Honor alone (see image).

!6FA5089C-6D5D-4F9B-A74F-0421AFB807E9.jpeg|width=414,height=159!

You can see the effect on result ordering with the following two searches for “comed” and “coméd”. In the following images, note the placement of Honoré de Balzac’s La Comédie Humaine. But it does appear in both cases\!

!A6766C22-B073-4EAC-A93E-2C6A5029C977.jpeg|width=414,height=430!

!2E6DC720-227A-4082-8D85-07DA7D75C90F.jpeg|width=414,height=431!

Another illustrative example is “Ángel” versus “Angel” (and other variations), which I tried in both Fandoms and Characters fields. I will attach some images which show the behaviour. Again, result ordering changes dramatically. 

!A5B42CF6-EFC9-434F-A1A1-68B7629B89E1.jpeg|width=414,height=403!

!52561A6E-7A23-42CE-8F3C-A215F0107638.jpeg|width=414,height=408!

!EF9F8F0A-49DC-4CAE-A6A0-5A9ED866B483.jpeg|width=414,height=405!

!CDD64887-E274-40B9-97C3-41B667FA5FC7.jpeg|width=414,height=310!

!9B7F5638-E60D-4927-9B8F-661E84B74034.jpeg|width=414,height=381!

!AEB5E883-0E97-499F-B288-9185CF5C11B7.jpeg|width=414,height=381!

Adding spaces and other strings (e.g. “Angel o” and variations, “Angel di” and variations) also makes results vary.

So I guess if the question is “does searching for a string with a non-matching diacritic now allow a tag with that string to show up in the autocomplete suggestions?” the answer is yes. However, if the question is “are diacritics now ignored by the autocomplete?” the answer is no.
column146:
30/Aug/21 8:04 AM;557058:bb48f715-7c87-43a5-81b8-a60c77a4c45b;Thank you for the super detailed response\!

I think most of it comes down to the highlighting (javascript) having not been updated to handle the diacritics.  I’ll make a separate Jira to address that and see what I can do.  As you deduced, the highlighting will only show when there’s an exact match including diacritics (same as current production), even though the updated autocomplete treats “élise” and “elise” equivalently under the hood.

So what should happen now, is that when you search (with or without diacritics) your result set will include tags both with and without diacritics based on some rudimentary matching (é = e, û = u, etc.) and then those search results will be ordered based on their score.  Other autocomplete behaviours should not have changed per se, though the results set is expanded due to the relaxed matching, and inputs may result in different suggestions because of that.  Specifically, fandom tags have different autocomplete behaviours than other tag types due to it being overridden in the model ([https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/tag.rb#L532|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/tag.rb#L532|smart-link]).  Also, when you put multiple words in the field, the searching takes that into account, so it’s not surprising that different characters as part of a second word give different suggestions.  These are existing behaviours and no changes to that were made as part of this effort.

again (AC options will come up but down arrowkey will not access them, though they
still can be selected by mouse.)

it to be accessed again), so this isn't a major concern, but it'd be helpful if mouse-clicking
back to the field also worked.

08/Sep/11 11:43 PM;557058:3564dbfd-03c5-46c9-9e5c-3219aea344c7;OK, I've basically written a master form layout which forces all inputs to be 100% of
their containing dd (which is normally 70% of its containing dl, which is normally
100% of its containing div, which is normally #main). #main with dashboard view (which
is what this is) is 100% of the page minus 15em, which is obviously a variable width
but seems to be functional at all the common screen sizes.

So to follow that through, at 800x640 and font-size 14px  you'd expect the input to
be about 340px or about 24.286em or about 48 characters. 1024 res gives you 70 characters
and 1280 res about 97. So this is better, I think. Obviously those char lengths will
decrease with text zoom, but we don't get down to the sizes you reported (20 chars)
until around maximum zoom on FF.

I've linearised the display for screens of max-width 480 (which is basically phones,
these days), but for people with larger screens deliberately making them VERY narrow,
they will still get some issues, but not as many. Back end have largely removed the
inconsistent hardcoded input sizing so that's not complicating the issue as much.

SO it's probably fixed on my webdev. Needs testing obv.

In terms of getting a 100% width at 800, (which I know you didn't ask for, this is
really for the benefit of other front end css coders who may be reading in the future
/me waves to them!) I don't think it's worth doing given the layout downsides for everyone
else (it would mean no 2-column forms). Our tags are extremely long and cause big problems
for layout in general; this is the best I can do right now balancing all the other
requirements: screen flexibility, semantic structure, dashboard view, font size, and
v. importantly, maintainable and readable CSS for the skinsers (I am NOT writing page
by page views into this layout; I am writing them OUT of this layout, they are to be
hunted down and generalised into zone rules).

!Screen Shot 2019-09-14 at 11.22.19 PM (29f3d385-719e-448f-9d22-6b00591e1964).png|width=1189,height=126!

*Testing*

# Log in

# Fill in the fields for the related work, including checking the “This work is a translation” box

column141:
23/Sep/13 4:02 PM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;External works can now be assigned languages, but apparently once assigned that language
cannot be changed.

Steps to replicate:

1) Go to Post > New work
2) Fill out fandom, tags, title, work text etc. and choose the language of your work
(TranslationLanguage)
3) Tick "This work is a remix, a translation, or was inspired by another work"
4) Enter the URL to an external work
5) Enter the Title and Author information
6) Choose a language from the popup to indicate what language the original work was
in (ExternalWorkLanguage)
7) Tick "This is a translation"
8) Post

Your Related works page now has an entry for the translation with "From ExternalWorkLanguage
to TranslationLanguage" in the Language column.

9) Realize you got ExternalWorkLanguage wrong
10) Edit your work and click "Remove" to remove the association (or use the "Remove"
link in the Related Works page)
11) Get Error 404

Your work now doesn't say it's a translation of anything.

12) Edit your work
13) Tick "This work is a remix, a translation, or was inspired by another work"
14) Enter the URL to the external work
15) Enter the Title and Author information as before
16) Choose the correct language for the external work (CorrectExternalWorkLanguage)
17) Tick "This is a translation"
18) Post

The translation link properly shows up on your work again.  _However_, the listing
on the Related Works page once again reads "From ExternalWorkLanguage to TranslationLanguage".

As far as I can tell, once an external work has been linked to once, that title/URL
combination is permanently locked to the language that was specified in that link.
 Even if you post a completely fresh work and try to give the external work its correct
language, you cannot change it.  If you use the same URL but tweak the title you link
with, you _can_ change it.

Ticket from a user who ran into the problem: https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/275761

They report being able to change this for two works from earlier this year but not
the latest two.  I don't know why this would be - I haven't been able to find any work-around
besides changing the title.

column1: Posting fill for prompt memes automatically fills all prompts by a user (sort of)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2433
1. Claim several different prompts from the same user on a prompt meme
2. Post to fulfill for one of these prompts.
3. Notice that under "Fulfill a Claim: " on the Post New Work page, that multiple prompts
are checked - any prompts by the same user (including any anonymously-submitted prompts)

Even if you uncheck all but the correct prompt, if you go back and edit the work after
posting you will see all the prompts re-checked. The only way to get it to stop checking
the prompts is to uncheck all of the prompts for the meme, post, and then edit to recheck
the correct one.  The only prompt acknowledged will be the first one checked; however,
this may *not* be the prompt you are actually trying to fill.

This is especially problematic because if a user happens to have submitted some anon
prompts and some public prompts, responses for the anon prompts can show as belonging
to that user.

(Oddly, the Fulfilled Claims at /collections/*/claims only shows the correctly filled
prompt, and the work will only show one "In response to a prompt by:" line in notes;
the problem is only really evident if you happen to have claimed an anon prompt and
a public prompt by the same user.)

(A work with the anon author problem here:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/214430
I posted this as a fill for the last (anon) prompt on the list; it treats it as a fill
for the first prompt.)

17:47:33">

Fixed by overriding the equality operator on challenge claims, and it all now works

All the media tags have a few of these false parent tags, and there's no way to remove them (removing the media from the fandom tag does not remove it from the parent tag list.) While they aren't causing any apparent trouble, they're a confusing artifact.

*Description of code changes:*

Currently, it's possible for wranglers to add invalid relationships (e.g. a Character tag that's the parent of another Character tag, or a Freeform that's the parent of a Relationship tag, or a non-canonical Character that's the parent of a canonical Relationship tag, or a tag that is its own parent). This pull request does several things to fix this:

# It adds two validation checks to the CommonTagging class: one to make sure that the parent tag is canonical, and one to make sure that the type combination of parent and child is allowed. This prevents the creation of new invalid relationships.
# It modifies the tag associations code so that new CommonTaggings are handled more like new MetaTaggings, but with error messages passed on to the user to make it clear why the CommonTagging/MetaTagging is invalid. It also uses Tag.parent_types in order to make sure that it handles all of the different types correctly (rather than having each tag type have its own version of add_association).
# It modifies the fandom_string/character_string/etc. code so that when you enter a tag of the wrong type, it will prevent the Tag from being saved and show an error message.
# It hides the mass "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" option on the fandom-specific Mergers page and the fandom-specific SubTags page, since that option isn't needed (and would always cause the creation of invalid wrangling relationships in the old system).
# It adds a task to destroy all invalid CommonTaggings, and a task to destroy all invalid MetaTaggings.
# It adds some rspec tests to make sure that the new code will add the associations it should, and show errors for the associations it shouldn't.

*Testing:*

It would be good to have several Tag Wranglers run the code through its paces -- go through their standard routine, and make sure that they don't get any unexpected errors. There are a lot more validity checks now than there were before, and it'd be good to make sure that none of them breaks any useful tricks currently used by the Tag Wrangling team.

So far we haven't noticed these weird relationships causing problems, and the parent/child

them is to de-canonize the tags and unhook all relationships, but for many tags (especially
large fandoms) this is...not an optimal solution.

column139:
07/Feb/14 5:47 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;To add a bit more detail about the fixes and what can now be expected: 

- The efiction chapter grabber will take a chunk (max 10,000 characters) from near
the start of the current chapter and compare it to the same chunk in the last chapter.
If they match, it will assume it has reached the end of the work and stop. This should
handle cases where an efiction site just gave the same content over and over when the
chapter # was incremented past the final chapter, which as far as I've been able to
see is the only cause of the endless chapters problem. 
 
-  Many efiction sites have a "broken" printable format where the <head> block doesn't
get closed. This causes the parsing to fail to find the chapter content. I have put
in a manual closing </head> to fix. 

Sites that are broken in different ways will not be fixed by this alas. 

Note: scarvesandcoffee.net does not have either of these issues and works fine in a
test of getting a 4-chapter work -- that would be a separate issue and I would need
a specific URL that isn't working to fix

whofic.com does have the endless identical chapters issue; that one should be fixed
and not get endless chapters anymore.

column142:
15/Feb/14 9:34 PM;557058:bc8b4996-2b30-4d70-8b0f-1e58eb680e17;I imported an eFiction work that had no warning popup and all 20 chapters were present
and it imported perfectly. I did some other tests with hiccups, but I think they're
unrelated; none of my tests yielded endless chapters, so I think this fix does what's
intended.

Other tests I did that might be relevant for other issues:
1. 21 chapter story:
- Only 16 of 21 were chapters imported, but chapter 17 was blank on the archive so
it probably confused the importer.
- In the preview of the work, the count shows 1/16 chapters. If you save it without
posting, the chapter count stays 1/16 even though you can navigate through the chapters
so it's only a visible blip. After posting, the count shows all 16 chapters as imported.
- As long as the chapter title was included in the work with "Title:" preceding it,
the chapter title was imported. If the chapter title wasn't prefixed with "Title:"
in the work, then the chapter title was imported as the title and author name of the
work.


I tried importing another work with 31 chapters that had a popup warning for mature
content. I tried once leaving the "&warning=4" appended to the end of the work URL,
and only the title, author name, and warning text was imported. I tried importing the
work without the "&warning=4" in the URL, but it still only imported the work title,
author name, and warning text. (The URL without the "&warning=4" in the URL goes directly
to the work without the warning popup, so I don't know how the importer 'found' the
warning.)
column143:
16/Feb/14 12:05 PM;557058:0670e11e-5036-4aae-af3f-d6ae02967b60;"In the preview of the work, the count shows 1/16 chapters. If you save it without posting,
the chapter count stays 1/16 even though you can navigate through the chapters so it's

Draft works and draft chapters are separate entities, so you always see 1/x  for a

the importer - normally without editing you can only see the first chapter of a draft
work with draft chapters.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Import http://spuffystuff.org/everytime.htm
2. Get a 500 error:

ArgumentError: unknown encoding name - macintosh

app/models/story_parser.rb:524:in parse_story_from_unknown'
app/models/story_parser.rb:514:in `parse_common'
app/models/story_parser.rb:180:in `parse_story'
app/models/story_parser.rb:152:in `download_and_parse_story'
app/controllers/works_controller.rb:554:in `import_single'
app/controllers/works_controller.rb:541:in `import'

That's with the site's own content encoding, "macintosh." We should catch that error
and inform the user so that they can set the encoding manually instead.

If you do set the encoding manually, however (using MacRoman from the dropdown list)
you'll see the same error message. (Other encodings don't get an 500 error, but will
naturally mess up the special characters.) My theory: "MacRoman" isn't known to Nokogiri,
thus it falls back to the "macintosh" declared in the document, which it fails on,
too.

We are getting the encodings list to choose from from the Encoding module, not from
Nokogiri. Seems that Nokogiri hast a slightly different list, we'll have to find out
if there's a way to get a list of encodings directly from Nokogiri.

column1: Cleaning up unused routes
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2504
We have many unused routes declared but never used. That is, when you declare

resources :foo

the following routes are automatically created:

index - foos
new   - foos/new
show  - foo/:id
edit  - foo/:id/edit 
and also create, update, and destroy. 

If any of these routes are not used, leaving them hanging around in the code unnecessarily
slows down the routing process, and also makes it harder to figure out the full set
of pages when needed for testing. So we should specify, for instance:

resources :foo, :only => [:index, :show]

if we only need those two routes. 


I have cleaned up a big bunch while making a rough site page listing.

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:

In user preferences, the values we store for timezones come from Rails, but Rails updates
them sometimes, so we need to handle the situation where the stored value isn't a valid
timezone. (Apparently they changed "Kyev" to "Kyiv" in 3.0, and when we started adjusting
dates based on preference timezones, the users with "Kyev" saved got a 500 error on
nearly every page.)

Also, while we're doing that, it would be good to cache the current user's timezone
as part of their session instead of accessing the preferences table wherever dates
appear. Dates appear a lot! :)

The said change in Rails is probably [https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/2e7409f035236c719c5b1567c4bb3e65a5e543bc|https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/2e7409f035236c719c5b1567c4bb3e65a5e543bc|smart-link]  , where the long name ("Europe/Kiev") was not changed. It might make sense to move away from the short name to the long name when storing in databases. With the long name, a massive migration is necessary once, but hopefully there will be less need to do so after that.

I'm not sure which is really better, though. It looks like the long name is not set in stone either, and has recently been changed (in 2022, in exceptional circumstances): [https://github.com/eggert/tz/commit/e13e9c531fc48a04fb8d064acccc9f8ae68d5544|https://github.com/eggert/tz/commit/e13e9c531fc48a04fb8d064acccc9f8ae68d5544|smart-link]  .

We'd need to take into account that some cities are not found in the long names. For UTC+9, there are Osaka and Tokyo and Asia/Tokyo (two cities in the same time zone), but there is no "Asia/Osaka". Anecdotally, as someone from the (larger) area, not having Osaka in the preferences is not a huge deal. But it may not be applicable to other cities.

04/Sep/11 12:11 PM;557058:be6d5da9-c318-4a37-90a3-f06f5f84c0eb;@myownconfusion: the cron job is currently running every hour on the hour on stage.
I expect to have it run more frequently in production once I see how long it takes
to run. I don't want them to run in parallel (one starting before the next finishes)
so I made the default pretty slow.

@xparrotx, it's not designed to update if you have reading history turned off. I think
you ran into a timing bug because the cron job is so infrequent. What happens is that
the fact that you've read a work gets put into redis, and then when the rake tasks
goes to see whether it should actually update your reading history it checks your preferences
at that time (not at the time you actually read it). Since the rake task is running
so infrequently, I believe you managed to turn your preference back on before the rake
task got around to those works. i don't think this is important enough to fix (let
me know if you disagree). 

both of you: I've updated testarchive to run the cron job every five minutes, which
should make it easier if you need to do any more testing :)

column1: Parser struggles with mixed uppercase & lowercase HTML
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2525
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the latest release notes in
http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts, for example 0.8.4.4). 0.8.8.0

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Post a work with some unevenly capitalised italics tags, like the file attached.

2. Preview and find that the italics are spread over paragraphs where they shouldn't
be

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

As far as I can see, when the parser encounters [i] it doesn't recognise [/I] as a
closing tag. So, it looks for the next [/i] - if this is several paragraphs away it
helpfully puts italics round all the intervening paragraphs. THEN the parser downcases
the offending [/I] (for extra confusion when you go back to edit mode). So, the original
italicised text looks normal, but several subsequent paragrphs are a mess. 

(Testing this with the attached will make this a lot easier to understand!)

In theory, this should be fixable by downcasing all HTML tags BEFORE the parser does
anything else. In practice, IDK if that will be possible. 


Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

<hr>

column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2554
Revisions to the tokeninput-based autocomplete based on fb from wranglers et al! This
is fixed as part of the tag sets update and will be pullreq'ed shortly. 


1) Arrow keys should now work intuitively. Here is my concept of intuitively :) 
* If there is something typed in the input box, the right and left arrow keys will
move you around in the input. If you edit/delete, the autocomplete search should fire
again & the results should reflect the changes. 

* If the dropdown menu is open, the up and down arrow keys will move you around in
the menu. If you are at the top and you press the up arrow, the topmost item should
be deselected (so that return will instead enter whatever you have typed in the input
box as a new tag), but the dropdown menu should remain open. (Escape key should continue
to close the dropdown.)

* If there is nothing typed in the input box, but there are tags added, the arrow keys
will move you among the added tags. Each arrow key should make the neighboring tag
selected. The input box should NOT move and the tags should remain displayed inline.
You should be able to delete tags via keyboard only without clicking with the mouse.

2) When you click out of the autocomplete field with text entered into it, the search
should NOT stop, and the text should NOT be added as a tag automatically. Instead,
the search should continue. When the results come back, you should be able to select
one. You should also be able to enter a new tag not on the list by hitting tab/enter/return/comma
at the end of the tag. 

3) It should be possible to paste in comma-separated items and each item should be
added as a separate tag, but unfortunately there isn't a good way to allow going in
mid-string and typing a comma as an edit without the comma triggering the adding of
the tag.

column1: Allow anonymous posting
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2562
Users should be able to post works (and series and prompts) anonymously, at a more fundamental
level than the current challenge anonymity system allows.

Proposed plan:
1) When posting or editing a work, the user can choose to make it anonymous.
2) Anonymous works are associated with an anon user account, not with the current user's
account, preventing the authorship from ever being revealed due to bugs.
3) Every anonymous work has an access key, and the original poster can use that key
to edit or delete the anonymous work or to de-anon and list the work under their own
name.
4) Anon works don't appear on the author's works list, but users should have a separate
area where they can view their keys and edit their works.
5) The user can choose to throw away the key, which is to say, delete the association
between their account and the work, losing their ability to edit/delete/claim but ensuring
that the work is permanently anonymous. Needs a workflow that will make it difficult
for people to do this accidentally. (See: many many support requests re: accidental
orphaning.)

Things to consider:
1) How this impacts our current orphaning feature.
2) How anonymous works will be handled by the abuse team. My instinct is that keys
should not be visible to site admins and should not be used when dealing with abuse
cases - otherwise they're not truly anonymous, and users should be made aware of that
- but we'll have to discuss it with Abuse and Content.
column129:
10/Jan/15 4:48 PM;557058:733fae5a-a08d-4a3b-91e0-914bfc0ce3a2;2) How anonymous works will be handled by the abuse team. My instinct is that keys should
not be visible to site admins and should not be used when dealing with abuse cases
- otherwise they're not truly anonymous, and users should be made aware of that - but
we'll have to discuss it with Abuse and Content.

If we went with this option, we'd need to make it very clear that users are giving
up their rights to defend themselves against any Abuse related charges. Abuse would
likely delete the work with minimal investigation; our hands would be tied since we'd
have no way to contact the user.

28/Oct/11 5:39 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;These are actually separate issues: the first one with the stacked icons has been fixed.


The second one with transparent icons is a side effect: to make all the archive icons
(including the default user icon) replaceable in skins, the icons have been moved into
CSS as backgrounds and therefore show even if the user has an icon of her own loaded
as an image on top. 

The workarounds currently available:
- users can upload opaque icons with their desired background if they want to control
what is in the background for other viewers.

- users can create a skin to replace the default user icon with a transparent one if
they want to see it transparent for themselves. The skin is a one-liner: 

.icon {background:transparent;}

If someone can test that one-liner skin to make sure it solves the problem, let's mark
this back to "Started" at low priority for a longer-term fix (which needs to be sure
not to break the skinnable icons!)- **Status changed**: `DeployedToTest`

31/Oct/11 5:24 AM;557058:3564dbfd-03c5-46c9-9e5c-3219aea344c7;/me pops head in to say because this is probably more useful logged somewhere 

Yep, we don't want alt text for background images, only content images. That is, we
don't want to describe "decorative left border graphic" or "blank/default user icon
space", we only want to communicate the content of graphics with non-visual meaning,
like "happy kitten smiles at you".

So there are places where we show "an icon" but it is just visually meaningful, like,
when a visitor comments on a story, who obviously has no icon, it shows our "default
icon" in that layout position, but it's meaningless in terms of content, so we don't
want to print an unecessary image there. In general we're working towards taking out
any hardcoded images, and using text there, specially for things like "left arrow"
or "close button", because styled text is really flexible, whereas pixel images are
less so.

Conceivably we might write a ton of exceptions on that .icon class for contexts where
we know there is a "content image" like a user-uploaded icon, and that may well be
the solution whoever picks this issue up goes with, but in general we want to keep
our css a lot simpler and not have so many page-specific rulesets, so it's easier for
users to adapt for their own use cases and for maintainability for us.

(So the concept for the teaching interface that is the styles, is that there's .icon,
which shows the default icon, and then we modify that image for different roles or
objects like: .collection .icon or .tag .icon, or .admin .icon . So I really want to
keep that simple so it's understandable. One option, which we had a go at already,
might be to figure out how to programmatically wrap that .icon in a .user div, but
that is bizarrely hard to do because it's inside out from the normal way)

All those icons are visual cues only, you don't want, say a screenreader reading out
"heading Collection page heading The Yuletide Collection Blank Collection Icon" or,
say, in a listing of tags, you don't want it to be like "heading Listing Tags ordered
list of 25 items list item 1 tag name Buffy the Vampire Slayer red square with a white
T centered" The tag icon is not especially related to the Buffy tag so it is not the
information you're looking for in that case and you pretty much know it's a tag already,
you don't want an alt there even just saying "tag".

People could exchange a sunflower for a penis, yes, just like they could in a work.
I imagine Abuse would deal with that, so maybe worth asking them if you're interested
in knowing more.

So yeah, really want to make as many images as possible skinnable, or "overridable"
so that people can use their own iconsets, maybe with different contrasts, or massive
or tiny, or different languages or symbol sets, or using ASCII symbols with scalable
pseudo content insertion, and of course I'm writing a ton of those so people without
css-skillz can more easily swap about.

OK hope this is helpful. Sorry it's not all better written etc - I'm no good at it!

was added. For example, right now the top discussion listed is:
jack abernathy	Jack Abernathy is an OMC created by a CSI: NY fa...	0	Vera		2011-10-26
19:28:23 -0400

But on the comment itself the date is: Posted Tue 16 Mar 2010 10:20PM EDT


This can be quite confusing, as if you don't check the date on the comment itself you
may not realize that the comment is old (and may not be applicable); it also means
the discussion page gets cluttered up with old comments.

I haven't been able to determine what exactly resets the dates - I have successfully
replicated the problem once on Test (by removing and adding fandoms and syn relationships),
but not consistently.
column129:
30/Aug/13 7:46 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;I have a suspect!

I suspect the content sanitiser. I have been able to make a very old comment show up
on the first page by simply *looking at it* - i.e. loading the comment.

If the content_sanitizer_version is older than the current ArchiveConfig.SANITIZER_VERSION,
the content will be sanitised *and saved*, thus possibly making the updated_at timestamp
jump to the time of loading the comment.

The Discussion page orders tag comments in 'updated_at DESC' order - not posted_at,
not edited_at.

(then click download, then EPUB)

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Download the EPUB from that page
2. Get EPUB Checker from http://www.rainwater-soft.com/epubchecker/
3. Validate the downloaded EPUB using the "preflight" tab.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

There should be no errors or warnings, but there are lots. The first one is the one
I'm talking about here:

ERROR: C:\Documents and Settings\Keith\My Documents\Downloads\Blue Skies over Bad Lands.epub:
mimetype contains wrong type (application/epub+zip expected)

Please provide any additional information below.

When an EPUB is created, the mimetype must be the first file in the archive. That's
correct in the AO3 Epubs. But it also has to be uncompressed.

Fortunately the fix for this should be trivial. The EPUB download code in app/controllers/downloads_controller.rb
has this as line 102:

    cmd = %Q{cd "#{@work.download_dir}/epub"; zip "#{@work.download_basename}.epub"
mimetype; zip -r "#{@work.download_basename}.epub" META-INF OEBPS}

..separating the zipping of mimetype from the other files to ensure that it's first.
All that needs to be done to fix this is to add a -0 to it to specify compression level
zero for that file.

    cmd = %Q{cd "#{@work.download_dir}/epub"; zip -0 "#{@work.download_basename}.epub"
mimetype; zip -r "#{@work.download_basename}.epub" META-INF OEBPS}

column132:
22/Mar/12 12:19 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;The icons and explanations are displayed as a definition list (dl), with the icon as
the definition term (dt) and the explanation as the definition (dd). By default, dl,
dt, and dd all display as block elements, meaning they stack on top of each other instead
of lining up side by side. 

There are two ways to view the symbols key and other help pages. The first way is in
a popup (ibox), which is how users with Javascript enabled will see this page when
they click a help link. The second way is on its own (like by visiting the URL above),
which is how users with Javascript disabled will see the page when they click a help
link.

This page is meant to be accessed through an ibox, and when it is, it displays with
the icons and explanations side-by-side. This is because the site stylesheets are applied
to the page on which the ibox appears (for instance, the works page), so the ibox content
(help page) inherits the stye information from the page it's on.

The way around this would be to add the style information to the help pages. There
are two ways to do that, but one of them (external stylesheets) is bad for performance
and another (embedded, in either the head or the elements themselves) is bad for both
accessibility and maintainability. Since the information is still understandable, this

column1: Allow collection owners/mods to add/invite works to their collections
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2668
What archive revision are you testing on? Beta 0.8.9.12

Currently there's no way for mods or owners to add works they haven't created to their
collections, short of waiting for authors to submit them, making the process of curating
collections more complicated.

The ideal feature would allow mods/owners to invite a work into their collection in
some manner, and then send the author a notice so that they can approve of it or not.


There's already a preference for authors to “Automatically agree to your work being
collected by others in the archive.” so if the author of the work has clicked it, the
mod's invitation would simply cause the work to be added to the collection.

(Second Image) The collection maintainer will see a message letting them know that they have successfully 'Invited' the work to join their collection. 21/Sep/12 3:19 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Right, those are unrelated. 

The statistics overlap can probably be fixed by adjusting the line height, although
I can't reproduce the problem on FF 15 on Mac OS X 10.8.2. The strange thing is the
amount of space between the text and the bottom border (we use borders, not underlines,
for accessibility reasons) -- for some reason, the space is much bigger on your browser
than on any of mine. Sam's screen shot is what it should look like.

Here's what's going on with the mis-aligned tags: the tags all have 0.25em of padding
on the left side to create a bit of breathing space. If the first word on a line is
the start of a new tag, it has 0.25em of padding on the left. If a multi-word tag wraps
to start a line, the padding is absent, so that line sticks out. The only way to fix
it is to remove the padding, but I'm not sure we want to sacrifice the white space,
which makes the tags easier to skim.

- skin cannot be in its own ancestry that is: 

Skin Grandparent parent of -> Skin Parent parent of -> Skin Child

I've un-floated actions in tables, which might help in some situations. It depends
on the size of your screen, default font, and/or browser window, and on the length
of the data in the table cells -- smaller screens or rows with longer data are always
going to have that stacking problem because the table cells just aren't wide enough
to keep everything on one line. 

The down side to this fix is that users with larger screens are now going to see headers
that are unnecessarily tall, since the actions will always appear beneath the text;
however, that's only one unnecessarily tall row, compared to what users of smaller
screens are currently seeing. 

So, try it, see if you like it. If it causes more problems than it solves, we'll make
this a WontFix instead.

sure it doesn't break any tables there.)- **Status changed**: `SubmittedPullRequest`
