column126:
14/Jan/12 9:58 PM;557058:a06b2e64-4893-491b-b85e-8176df5059b9;from Facet:
Hey, there.

I was reading an article about using overflow: hidden and floated content and it made
me remember the funky bug with the user fandoms list disappearing if you take off the
border. I see there’s a second one about that being the case in One Point Faux.

The issue is a known hazard of setting overflow:hidden (which .listbox has) and people
always used to set a width on elements to make it work correctly in older browsers.
This practice has fallen off as browsers have improved.

I tested One Point Faux and the default skin with #user-fandoms {border: 0; width:
100%} and there was no disappearing content. So setting width: 100% on either .listbox
if that won’t screw anything else up or on #user-fandoms alone will let anyone do what
they want with borders on that element.

Hope this helps.

(and maybe elsewhere?) where we make disctinctions between the type of commentable:
"commentable.is_a?(Tag)" or "when /Tag/", mostly to get paths to commentable instances

change quite a few places in the comments_helper and comments_controller.

etc) to the commentable class vendor/plugins/acts_as_commentable/lib/commentable_entity.rb
and then overwrite those methods in the individual models, like it's already done for
the commentable_name and commentable_owner methods.

coder who likes to have a look at backend code design.

Either of these changes will require the secondary step of adding #footer .secondary li a:hover to make the skin chooser links (i.e. the names of the skins) readable in hover mode. What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Go to the home page (or any page) 
2. Navigate through links using tab key (tab+option on Mac)

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
When navigating a site using the keyboard, the link or input field you are currently
paused on gets a special style, defined with the pseudo-class :focus. We currently
have a:focus defined as {outline: 1px dotted}, which means focus is shown with an outline
the same color as the link text. This is a problem because the focus in the header
is indicated with a dark, dotted outline -- nearly invisible on the background image.
At the least, we need to make this stand out for users who navigate via keyboard.

Please provide any additional information below.

Relevant portions of bug report:

When navigating in the current default skin, the outline around buttons--the navigation
buttons in the header, the edit and edit tags buttons on my own works, etc.--is not
displayed consistently and is at times nearly or completely invisible.

In the header, the outline shows around the button itself in black on a red textured
with black ground (this is nearly invisible). But on the search button, the text is
enclosed, not the button, so it is visible.

Interestingly, in Reversi, (the white on blackish) skin the problem is, er, reversied.
The buttons in the header are now outlined white on black, except search which is black
on the dark button around the text and is nearly invisible.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
The CSS area only displays about ten lines of text at a time, which is especially frustrating
given its tendency to display every element on its own line. The CSS textarea should
be bigger, like the same size as the Work Text textarea: http://archiveofourown.org/works/new

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.
The size of the story textarea is currently defined in 07-interactions.css with .post
.text textarea { height: 36em; clear:right} in the section called "INTERACTION: POST."

The CSS textarea can be targeted through textarea #skin_css or .edit_skin textarea,
but it does not need clear: right, nor does it belong in the same section as .post
.text textarea. To implement this, we would need something like .edit_skin textarea
{ height: 36em; }. In the spirit of DRY, I'm thinking it would be better to set { height:
36em; } up as its own class, since we will probably want other large textareas elsewhere
in the future -- something like textarea .large { height: 36em;}. The large class can
be added to the relevant textareas as needed, and height: 36em can be removed from
.post .text textarea in 07-interactions.css.

not alerted in any way when they are added, so may never know.

h1. Original issue

*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2780*
otwarchive test-0.8.10.12

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1. Have a story posted on the archive
2. Have another version of the story archived on AO3 from a different site (e.g. the Yuletide archive gets imported, after you have already uploaded your previous Yuletide stories to AO3.)

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

I would expect some way to combine the different copies, or at least a warning message and explanation of what to do.  Ideally there would be a way to move comments/hitcounts/community associations from one version to the other - but since we don't have a way to do that (yet?) at least explain that the copy of the story can be claimed and deleted. (Mention it in the email invitation and claims page?)

It also might be useful to provide a link for adding the existing AO3 story to the archivist's collection, or some other way to replace an imported story with an existing AO3 copy?

(Considering the number of authors who have uploaded their past Yuletide stories to AO3, there are going to be a lot of people contacting Support about this unless it's clearly explained.  Not to mention the Smallville Slash Archive - I've got a dozen stories posted there myself that are already up on AO3, would like to have some way to manage this.)

h1. Spec from Open Doors:

*Feature request:* A tool that can be used to combine the stats and additional attributes of two AO3 works into a chosen body of work (W-original), by inputting two work URLs.

*Essential*
1. The user of the tool selects the work they want to keep (W-original), and the one they want to merge into it (W-dupe). All the components from W-dupe that are not editable (comments, kudos, and hit counts) will be added to W-original (on top of any comments, kudos, and hits it has already). 

2. Any co-author on either one of the works will be added to the final work.

*Desirable:*
1. This will be a self-service tool that checks to see if the logged-in account owns the works in question. 

2. The URL of the merged work should be the URL of the W-original.

3. The tool should keep the merged work in any collection or series either copy was part of. 
For example, if W-original is part of the collection "Clark/Lex Funtimes" and W-dupe is part of "Smallville Slash Archive", the combined work (W-original-merged) should appear in both collections.

4. Any bookmarks made on W-dupe will be transferred and link to W-original. 

5. Any redirects pointing to W-dupe will automatically point to W-original. 
For example, redirects were set up for the Smallville Slash Archive. If "[http://smallville.slashdom.net/w-dupe|http://smallville.slashdom.net/w-dupe]" redirects to W-dupe on AO3, it will redirect to W-original on AO3 after the merge.

6. The URL for W-dupe should automatically redirect to W-original.

7. The merge tool page should include a reminder that if the user of the tool wants to keep any editable attributes (like ratings or tags on the work, and inclusion in any collections if this is not part of the tool) of W-dupe, they should add it themselves to W-original before merging the works.

8. After combining the works, W-dupe is deleted.

column1: Wrangler page allows you to assign non-canonical fandoms to yourself (but not remove them)
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2785*
otwarchive test-0.8.10.12

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Go to the edit page for a non-canonical fandom tag, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/The%20100/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/The%20100/edit]
# Follow the “Sign Up” link to go to the Tag Wrangling Assignments page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers]) with the fandom listed under “Assign fandoms to yourself”
# Press “Assign” to create the assignment

*What actually happens?*

The assignment is created and the fandom appears on your wrangler assignment page.

However, if on the /tag_wranglers page you filter for yourself using the "Show Only Wrangler" option, the non-canonical fandom tag will not appear, so there is no way to unassign it from yourself. (You can work around this by canonizing the tag, unassigning it, and de-canonizing the tag again).

*What should happen?* 

You should not be able to assign non-canonical fandoms to yourself. This means: 

* There should not be a “Sign Up” link on the edit page for non-canonical fandoms.
* Entering a non-canonical fandom directly in the “Assign fandoms to yourself” field and pressing “Assign” should not create the assignment. (If you enter a nonexistent or non-fandom tag in this field, it fails silently while giving a success message. There’s no need to fix that as part of this issue – we can live with the misleading success message and silent failure for this as well.)

Please also include a rake task to destroy any existing wrangling assignments for non-canonical fandoms.

h2. Deploy

25/Jan/12 4:52 AM;557058:209c080a-c6d9-49fa-bd8e-265199e385aa;Possible bottlenecks to consider:

1) This is only an issue when sorting by fandom, but paginate_by_sql is a lot slower
than the ordinary paginate. I don't think there's any easy way round this.

coll.prompts.where("type = 'Request'").order("id DESC").paginate(:page => 1, :per_page

0.078842

effectively doubling the database load here. Could we look at a paginate option that

SELECT `prompts`.* FROM `prompts` WHERE (`prompts`.collection_id = 1034) AND (type
= 'Request') ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5 OFFSET 0;

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `prompts` WHERE (`prompts`.collection_id = 1034) AND (type = 'Request');

column129:
21/Oct/12 11:28 PM;557058:af30f590-7d24-4a9b-81cf-7481873c80f3;For the fandom sorting, we can replace the paginate_by_sql with this:

      @requests = @collection.prompts.where("prompts.type = 'Request'").
                              where("tags.type = 'Fandom'").
                              joins(:tag_set => :tags).
                              order("tags.name #{@sort_direction}").
                              paginate(:page => params[:page])

I haven't tested on a large data set to see if it's actually faster. Note that both
this query and the current one give non-deterministic sorting order if a prompt has
more than one fandom. Existing implementation just joins with fandoms and then does
GROUP_CONCAT on fandom names, so whatever ordering we're getting in fandoms within
a prompt (like "Fandom B, Fandom A, Fandom C") is incidental and not guaranteed. Likewise,
this new implementation just takes the "first" fandom for a prompt, whatever MySQL
decides that is, and uses it for sorting. To have alpabetic sorting within prompts
we'd have to add a subquery to the SQL, which might not be possible if we go to the
non-paginate_by_sql solution.

doesn't allow for much tuning. It automatically queries the total count and there's
not a way to turn that off. Based on what I've read, getting later pages is always
going to be slower, especially using the InnoDB table storage engine (not sure which
we're using). If we need to optimize by not showing the page count, we should look
into turning all the challenge request index queries into ones we specify ourselves
not using the gem.

column126:
14/Jan/12 9:58 PM;557058:a06b2e64-4893-491b-b85e-8176df5059b9;From Facetofcathy:
Hey, there.

I was reading an article about using overflow: hidden and floated content and it made
me remember the funky bug with the user fandoms list disappearing if you take off the
border. I see there’s a second one about that being the case in One Point Faux.

The issue is a known hazard of setting overflow:hidden (which .listbox has) and people
always used to set a width on elements to make it work correctly in older browsers.
This practice has fallen off as browsers have improved.

I tested One Point Faux and the default skin with #user-fandoms {border: 0; width:
100%} and there was no disappearing content. So setting width: 100% on either .listbox
if that won’t screw anything else up or on #user-fandoms alone will let anyone do what
they want with borders on that element.

Hope this helps.

column129:
28/Aug/12 8:29 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;How this works: 

You add a work to a moderated, unrevealed or anon collection and it will be unrevealed
or anon despite not yet being approved by the collection mod.

If the collection mod rejects the work, it will remain unrevealed until (a) you edit
the work to remove the collection or (b) the collection mod removes it from the collection
or (c) the collection mod unchecks the unrevealed box.

If the collection mod approves the work, it will stay unrevealed until (a) you edit
the work to remove the collection or (b) the collection mod unchecks the unrevealed
box.
column132:

has been removed from it. Removing the collection information from a accepted work
makes it visible. Revealing the challenge makes the works visible (including rejected
ones). \o/

Anon: story posted appear anon before acceptance/rejection. Rejection does not make
the story become non-anon, but removing the collection info does.  
However, rejected items appear to remain anon after the collection as a whole is revealled...

column129:
22/Nov/12 5:25 PM;557058:a04c228c-7d70-4967-8583-25de929b4720;An easy fix would be to add a regex check (for "-SOMETHING-"+term) on each user-defined
properties, rather than only checking for exact equality.

This should be safe, as user-defined values which pass can only be one of our allowed
properties, an vendor version of one of our allowed properties, or an invalid property.

It also avoids the huge amount of repetition involved in including prefixed properties
in SUPPORTED_CSS_PROPERTIES.

The downside is that we'd be allowing invalid properties (eg: "-moz-color"). But by
allowing any vendor properties, we'll be allowing invalid properties anyway, so I don't
think that should really matter.

column27:

The Devise gem is a popular option for authentication with Rails 3: https://github.com/plataformatec/devise

It includes some functionality that we've implemented ourselves; if we migrated, that
would be code that we didn't need to maintain, and using a well-supported tool with
a large community behind it would have some security upsides. I also suspect that migrating
the users table over wouldn't be very difficult, and there are some good options available
for integrating it with Omniauth. 

(My recommendation is that we should do it: I've used it on other projects, and it
works great. I feel like the security and maintainability gains make it worth doing
even though migrating will be more work than installing it in a new app, which takes
about 5 minutes.)

column127:
11/Mar/12 8:13 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;It's the same on work blurbs, with <h4 title="title"> surrounding "Work Name by Author."
Likewise, <dl title="stats"> surrounds all the stats. 

I think the reason we do it this way is so people who hear the title from their screen
readers will hear "Name: Collection Name (collection_name) by Collection Owner" rather
than "Collection Title: Collection Name Collection Name: (collection_name) by Collection
Owner: Collection Owner," which would get supremely annoying on a page that lists 20
collections, some with multiple owners (so, if the title attribute were applied to
the link, which is the alternative, you'd get "Collection Title: Collection Name Collection
Name: (collection_name) by Collection Owner: Collection Owner 1, Collection Owner:
Collection Owner 2...") The word 'by' is a fairly good indicator of owner or authorship.

Giving each item in the h4 its own title would almost certainly fall under the category
of title attribute abuse: http://www.rnib.org.uk/professionals/webaccessibility/wacblog/Lists/Posts/Post.aspx?id=38

I'm going to say this is a WontFix.

column133:
16/Nov/12 7:13 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;So unfortunately, this is wrong. :( 

PromptMeme maintainers should NOT be able to edit prompts. 

The only reason GiftExchange maintainers are allowed to edit is in order to allow them
to successfully create matches. What often happens in a GE is that after signup is
closed, it's discovered that a participant can't be matched; they have to be asked
for changes. 

However, opening signup to allow them to make those changes would also allow other
people to come in and make changes and sign up even after it's supposed to be closed,
thereby potentially introducing NEW issues with matching. 

In practice, therefore, it is necessary to allow this editing, and the participants
also get a check on this because they then in fact end up assigned, so if the maintainer
has changed their signup to something weird, they will find out when they get their
gift! :P 

In a PromptMeme, this consideration doesn't arise. If a prompt is inappropriate, the
maintainer should be able to delete it, but not edit it.

column1: Gift Exchange Challenge: Potential matches are too slow
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2869
Generating potential matches for a large challenge with many settings is a performance
drain and takes an undesirably long amount of time. 

Instead of generating potential matches in a batch, potential matches should be generated
by-user, as signups are added, edited, and removed.
column130:
29/Oct/13 8:19 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;More detail on this issue: 

The underlying problem is that potential matches were being generated by exhaustively
comparing every signup against every other signup in the challenge, even if that was
not necessary (because the two signups didn't share any tags) and even if the signup
already had a massive list of potential matches. 

Instead, we now only compare signups that share at least one tag of a type required
for matching by the challenge (that is, if you have to match on fandom, signups are
only compared if they share at least one fandom tag), and potential matches are cut
off after a top limit (currently 50). 

This drastically speeds up matching. For instance, Yuletide with 1800 participants
was taking ~3 days for matching to run under the old system; under the new process,
it takes ~15 hours instead. 

IN ADDITION, if people turned up who had no potential matches, after getting more offers/requests
from those people, potential matches had to be regenerated for the ENTIRE challenge.
The new process now allows a mod to regenerate potential matches just for a single
person without throwing out all the old matches. 

Testing this sadly requires: 
- creating a collection and gift exchange challenge 
- in the gift exchange settings it would be great to try a variety of "required" settings
-- note that the "yuletide" option of 1 fandom and all characters is really well exercised
in the automated tests, and I have done a lot of testing with a challenge of 1 character
and 1 freeform required, so other combinations would be great to try. 
- having multiple people sign up with various options, some matching and some not
- have at least one person sign up who doesn't match anyone else
- close signup and generate potential matches from the "Matching" page in the collection
sidebar

You should see: 
- potential match generation progress should show correctly (you should see a name
listed and a % of the way through the challenge when you refresh the page)
- after potential matches are generated you should see the person who didn't match
anyone else listed separately
- you should be able to edit their signup, make them match, and then regenerate potential
matches for them
- after their potential matches are generated, you should be able to regenerate assignments

I have also tried to clean up the page, break out a lot of the (ugly) view code into
partials, and move the too-wordy and confusing instructions into a single help file
with more context and explanation. Any suggestions for further improving the help very
welcome!

06/Sep/13 9:36 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;The fix for this is pretty simple -- just take out the validation. Nothing actually
gets hurt by a tag set association duplicating a canonical association. :P 

How to reproduce the bug (steps must happen in this order): 

1) Nominator nominates fandom Foo and character Bar, both new
2) TagMod approves the nomination, so Foo and Bar now exist as AO3 tags
3) Wrangler wrangles Bar into Foo
4) TagMod goes to the "Review Association" page and sees [Bar —> Foo] as an association
that needs to be added (because they were not canonically associated when the noms
were created)
5) TagMod tries to approve this association and gets an error message because the association
is already canonical, and the association sits there on the page immovably

(Side note for testing, Nominator/TagMod/Wrangler can all be the same user, you don't
have to swap accounts!)

After this fix, the association SHOULD be approved in step #5, and then vanish off
the Review Associations page. 

Other things to confirm: Bar should only be listed under Foo once in the tag set, and
only appear once in the autocomplete for a challenge under Foo. (I have confirmed these
myself.)  

Will submit pullreq later tonight but wanted to add this info now.

10/Sep/13 10:03 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;For Issue 3743, associations weren't appearing until Edit & Update because the tag set
sweeper didn't run when reviewing nominations. I assume the problem here is the tag

column138:
14/Sep/13 10:56 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;OK, duh, sorry, I had misunderstood LO's comment here and was mightily confused, because
the tag set sweeper is in fact . 

The behavior LO saw (the association vanishes after the tags are wrangled) was NOT
the case in the original issue, which, it turns out, was already fixed in a different
way. The tag_sweeper updates tag nominations to mark them as parented, which is why
the tag set associations now (correctly) vanish from the tag set associations page.


So, this code change could in fact be pulled out, but I'm inclined to leave it. 

There is a DIFFERENT issue here, which is that the tag set view cache does not expire
when a tag in a set is wrangled. That is a totally different bug and would affect many
other scenarios as well, eg, if a tag is added to an additional fandom, removed from
one, etc., regardless whether or not the tag wasn't canonical before.  

I could fix this separate issue -- it would involve the tag sweeper checking for and
expiring owned tag sets that the wrangled tag is inside. It could in fact be a performance
hit -- so IDK if we want to do it, and if we want to do it for this deploy. I think
probably break out the issue and skip it. It is in fact broken this same way on beta
and has been.

http://archiveofourown.org/works/new

There are duplicate and non-canonical tags appearing in the autocomplete - for example,
if you type in "Norse" in the fandom field, you will see both "Norse Mythology" (the
canonical) and "Norse Mythology - Fandom", despite there being no tag on the Archive
"Norse Mythology - Fandom".  (see: http://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&query%5Bname%5D=Norse+Mythology+-+Fandom&query%5Btype%5D=Fandom
)

It seems like this happens when an admin edits a tag - the autocomplete continues to
list the old tag wording, not the new one.

For instance, on test, if an admin edits the tag Supernatural (http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Supernatural%20-%20Fandom/edit)
to "Supernatural - Fandom", it will still be listed as "Supernatural" on the autocomplete.
If a user then selects "Supernatural" from the autocomplete, it will create a new,
unwrangled tag.

This is not that big a problem for the works and bookmark autocompletes, which don't
care whether or not a tag is canonical, but it is an issue with the tag wrangling interface
and challenges, which sometimes require users to select canonical tags - the tag will
appear as a canonical in the autocomplete, but will be unusable when the user attempts
to save. It also can create duplicate fandoms - if the new unwrangled tag is canonized,
a new entry will be added to the autocomplete for it, ignoring the old entry.  (e.g.
if after changing the Supernatural tag to "Supernatural - Fandom", you then create
a new tag "Supernatural" and canonize it,  "Supernatural" will appear twice in the
autocomplete, though either one will link to the same tag.)

column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2922
The CSS portion of the help box changes for Issue 1190 (pull request #500) needs some
tweaks, which I've outlined in a comment on the pull request (https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/500#issuecomment-4187839)
and will copy below. 

Since the pull request was already merged, Elz suggested I create an issue here so
we can make sure it gets taken care of.

=

1. #ibox_w
 * Unless there are problems with IE, this should be fine with just top or bottom and
right or left, not all four
 * Since filter: Alpha(Opacity=60) and -ms-filter: Alpha(Opacity=60) are just for older
versions of IE, they should be moved to the IE stylesheets (they should also written
entirely in lowercase)
 * Actually, the filter: alpha(opacity=60) version should cover everything from IE8
down, so the prefixed version can just be removed

2. #ibox_w, #ibox_wrapper
 * Since these are CSS3 properties, each line should be indented by four spaces, and
there should only be a single space before the value

3. #ibox_content
 * The width and height are both defined twice here -- I think you meant to set them
just to inherit
 * The margin, padding, and positioning are all defined in pixels and should, if at
all possible, be changed to ems so users who've set a larger font size don't run into
trouble
 * The padding might look better if it was set on all four sides, so longer content
doesn't run directly up against the footer and scroll bar

4. #ibox_footer
 * The bottom position should also be changed to ems

Also, it's probably okay to delete the "todo: REPLACE WITH KBD LIGHTBOX)" portion of
the comments, since you've made them work with the keyboard now. \o/

27/Feb/12 12:42 AM;557058:a04c228c-7d70-4967-8583-25de929b4720;Hi Sarken, thanks for the review!  I'll try to make these changes today or tomorrow.

re: #3, I set the w&h twice because IE7 doesn't recognize "inherit", and skipped the
bottom and right padding for the same reason - if w&h=100%, ibox_content just grows
outside the container which looks weirder the more padding you add.  Should I still

column126:
27/Feb/12 1:03 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;Not a problem! We use conditional stylesheets, so we can give it two styles without
favoring anyone.

Let's say #ibox_content { width: inherit; height: inherit; padding: 0.643em; } works
fine in all browsers except IE7. That's fine. It can go in 07-interactions.css, which
all browsers will use. Then, to make it work in IE7, you would add #ibox_content {
width: 100%; height: 100%; padding-bottom: 0; padding-right: 0; } to 31-role-ie7.css,
and that would fix by overriding the problem areas for IE7.

(You might also want to try setting width and height to auto and seeing if that works
better than inherit and 100%. I don't think it will, but it could be worth a try.)

Skins and Invitations work like that, too. Or, well, Invitations would, too, if I hadn't
been a dingbat and forgotten to include a link to http://sarken.archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations
in the menu. Oops. I will add that; it's just a tiny bit important.

Basically, it works like that because the top-most links on the admin menu are the
same URLs as links for menu items (Approval Queue and Skins are the same, Admin Posts
and AO3 News are the same, Invitations and Invite Users will be the same), and drop
down menus don't appear if the top-most link is the current page. To illustrate, if
you go to http://test.ao3.org/menu/browse the Browse menu doesn't appear if you hover
over it. That page and the others like it exist for users who are navigating with a
keyboard and with Javascript disabled -- you can't access items in a drop down menu
with a keyboard unless there is Javascript. However, there was no existing page that
offered the options contained within the Browse drop down menu, so one had to be created.

I didn't make pages like http://test.ao3.org/menu/browse for the admin pages because
if you go to AO3 News, for example, the same items that are contained in the Admin
Posts drop down menu are available right from that page (Post AO3 News, Archive FAQ,
Known Issues) in the existing navigation, so the extra pages would just be redundant
and throw in an extra step for any admins who used keyboard navigation with Javascript
disabled. I can add http://test.ao3.org/menu/browse style pages for the admin area
or I can get rid of the drop down menus and leave it the same as beta, which might
actually be more convenient for everyone. I wasn't really sure which admins would prefer,
and, as you can see, it's a little hard to explain, so I figured it was best to just

NOTES ON WHERE SCROLLTO JAVASCRIPT WORKS:

The function that takes you to the top of paginated comments http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=2812
only works in some instances.

In theory, clicking the bottom pagination should be taking you to #comments_placeholder,
which is beneath the comment form. If this were successful, the comments' top pagination
would be at the top of your screen. 

In reality, try the following. This uses a general audiences-rated work to avoid any
problems that might come from the adult content warning. We're using beta to observe
the existing behavior.

==

1.  Follow this link to a work with paginated comments: http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867

Now, click the Comments (#) link on the bottom of the work to reveal the comments and
the comments pagination. Use either the top or bottom pagination links to travel to
the second page of comments. Notice that the top pagination is the topmost item in
your browser window. 

This is the desired effect. We use jQuery to make the pagination scroll to #comments_placeholder,
a container whose first visible item is the top pagination. It works because we're
loading the next page of comments with Ajax.

Close that window or tab.


2. Now, follow this same link to the same work with the same paginated comments: http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867

This time, click the Comments link on the top of the work. This causes the page to
reload with both the comment parameters and the comment anchor appended to the URL.
Your address bar will say http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867?show_comments=true#comments
and the kudos will be the topmost item in your browser window. This is because #comments
refers to an invisible page anchor in the invisible h3 element above the kudos section.

Now use either the top or the bottom pagination to travel to the second page of comments.
Notice that you are at the top of the work. 

This is the desired effect. This is the same behavior that users with Javascript disabled
will always see, regardless of which comment link they use. This behavior is not broken,
although we may wish to modify the pagination links to include the #comments anchor
in this instance.

It is not possible to reproduce the effect from (1) here because we are loading a new
page rather than using Ajax.

29/Dec/22 9:14 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;Hey [~accountid:557058:48d6a38e-168b-4aa7-a58d-a1853a844295]! Sorry this issue is pretty light on details, but there are a few things we need to discuss and figure out before moving ahead with it.

In terms of format, there are 2 approaches we thought about:

* A big zip file with all the works inside - mobile devices may not handle the format well (iOS can open them, Kindles likely not.)
* A big HTML file that covers all the works, then converted to other formats with Calibre/wkhtmltopdf, just like works - this requires either adding complexity to the existing work download layout, or adding a new series download layout.

And then there’s the issue of size: since we generate downloads on demand, we are already getting user reports of downloads that timed out because the works are too big. Series download would run into that problem more frequently. We thought about:

* Generating downloads in the background, similar to e.g. Twitter tweets archives. This requires significant UI design work (so users can check on status, be notified, etc.)
* Generating downloads on post / save instead of on demand. Also an asynchronous process, although not triggered by users. This requires some UI rework (e.g. buttons that say “downloads still generating, check back soon!“ maybe?)

column1: Ability to recategorize bookmark tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2941
Tag wranglers need the ability to change the category of bookmark-only tags (tags used
only on bookmarks/external works). (Currently all new bookmark tags are put in freeforms,
but users often mark fandoms/ships/chars in bookmark tags as well.)

Feature: bookmark-only tags appear as 'Unsorted Tags'.  Unsorted tags can have their
category changed to fandom/relationship/character/freeform as needed, either on the
Unsorted Tags page or on the individual Tag Edit page.

If a tag's category is changed, it can be changed back to Unsorted or to another category,
as long as it still has not been used on any works or drafts. Once a tag has been used
on a work or draft, its category can no longer be changed.  Unsorted tags cannot be
wrangled (synned, canonized, or added to fandoms) and a syn/canonical tag (even with
0 uses) cannot have its category changed unless it is unsynned/de-canonized.

Unsorted tags should still work the same as all unfilterable tags (bringing up attached
bookmarks as expected). (Do they appear in Search?)

When an unsorted tag is moved to a category, it should appear in the mass-wrangle bins
(unless it was previously a categorized tag and had a fandom assigned).  Tags categorized
as Fandom tags should automatically be added to the Uncategorized Fandoms media.

The Unsorted page shows only 25 uncategorized tags at a time; there may be more in
the system, which will appear once the displayed tags are categorized.

column1: Marking unwrangleable tags
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column27:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2943
Wranglers want a way to mark "unwrangleable" tags (those tags in the unfilterable section
of a fandom that for whatever reasons will never be made into a canonical or syn, so
can be safely ignored by the wranglers.) Please note: "unwrangleable" is different
from "unwrangled" (which indicates a tag not yet assigned to a fandom.)

Unwrangleable tags should be able to be both marked and unmarked by any wrangler. Only
non-canonical, non-synned tags should be able to be marked (synning or canonizing an
unwrangleable tag should either be impossible or else automatically unmark it.)

Ideally, unwrangleable tags should be able to stay in their appropriate fandom.  However,
they should not appear in the unfilterable counts for that fandom (that is, when a
wrangler goes to their homepage, e.g. http://archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/Xparrot
, tags marked unwrangleable should not appear in the counts under 'unfilterable'.)
(If there isn't a good way to do this, making unwrangleable tags all under a non-displayed
fake 'fandom' instead would also work.)

Unwrangleable tags should function exactly like unfilterable tags to users.  They should
still be findable in search, and be visible to wranglers somewhere - either in a general
mass-wrangle page showing all unwrangleable tags on the archive, or on the mass-wrangle
page of a fandom (e.g. http://archiveofourown.org/tags/GetBackers/wrangle?show=relationships
) - another list, along with canonical/non-canonical/etc? (We need to be able to see
them so we can make sure tags that can in fact be wrangled don't end up there!)

The form should look similar to the edit form for a single work (e.g. http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/284072/edit)
with:
1. a legend, 
2. a landmark (visible in skins that display landmarks or by viewing the page source;
also available to screen readers)
3. a single line under each form label 
4. the Cancel option styled as a button (like the Update option next to it)
5. the character counter right-aligned under the corresponding text field
6. the text fields with character counters should also have Live Validation (the red
writing that pops up when you're over the character count)

Instead, there are 
1. no legends
2. no landmarks 
3. the form labels in the second fieldset have double underlines
4. the Cancel option is a plain text link
5. the character counter is centered under the corresponding input
6. the text fields with character counters do not have Live Validation

tl;dr: the series edit page was overlooked in the massive overhaul of late 2011

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.
column125:
11/Mar/12 6:54 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/526

1. The legend is included, but you'll have to view the source (per our style, forms
with three of fewer fieldsets do not display legends) -- the line you are looking for
is <legend>Meta</legend>.

2. The landmark is not included, as it was an experiment on the works form.

3. Form labels now have only one line beneath them.

4. The Cancel option is style as a button.

5. The character counter is now right-aligned.

6. If you go over the character limit, the red Live Validation text will appear.


Additionally:
 
7. The form is now two fieldsets (grey boxes) instead of three. I did this for two
reasons. One, because it corresponds with how the information is displayed. The information
provided for Series Title, Author/Pseuds, Co-authors, Add co-authors?, Series Description,
Series Notes, and This series is complete, all displays as one group on the series
page (the meta box above the stories). Two, because it corresponds with the way forms
are laid out elsewhere on the site. The forms for collections and works both put title,
authors/owners, summary/description, and notes in a single fieldset.

8. The checkbox now appears to the right of the label 'This series is complete' rather
than appearing to the left of the label 'Is this series complete?' It might seem visually
counterintuitive, but it tends to work better for assistive technology, and we use
this layout in many forms. 


Known issues:

a. Ticking the Add co-authors? box does nothing. See Issue 2614.

b. When viewing the form for a series that has a co-author, the 'Current Co-authors:'
label has a colon, unlike all the other labels. This will be fixed when the forms are
all properly standardized.- **Status changed**: `SubmittedPullRequest`

no one can bookmark them. We want to increase the field length from 500,000 to 510,000
to compensate for that, but leave the Javascript live validation at 500,000 so that
there's space for the parser to add paragraphs to new works.

(Will have to check and see if the broken works are in the seed data - if not, we'll
have to fake something up for testing.)
